title: Skeletal Mesh Retargeting Preview with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a skeletal mesh retargeting preview system with particle effects. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e) with a ground plane (20x20, color 0x2d2d44, semi-transparent 0.6 opacity).
- Camera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (5, 10, 5).
- Two humanoid stick-figure skeletons side by side: a 'source' skeleton at x=-2 and a 'target' skeleton at x=2.
- Each skeleton is built from THREE.Bone hierarchy: root(hip) -> spine -> chest -> head, and hip -> leftLeg -> leftFoot, hip -> rightLeg -> rightFoot, chest -> leftArm -> leftHand, chest -> rightArm -> rightHand. Visualize bones using small spheres (radius 0.08) at joints connected by thin cylinders (radius 0.02) for limb segments. Source skeleton colored 0x00aaff, target colored 0xff6600.
- The source skeleton has a different scale: it is 1.5x taller than the target (source total height ~3.0 units, target ~2.0 units).

## Animation System
- The source skeleton plays a looping walk cycle animation. Implement procedurally: legs alternate forward/back sinusoidally, arms swing opposite to legs, spine has slight forward lean oscillation. Use elapsed time with a configurable speed multiplier (default 1.0).
- A 'retarget' system maps source bone rotations onto the target skeleton, compensating for the scale difference. The target should mimic the source motion but at its own proportions.
- Retargeting has a blend factor (0.0 to 1.0, default 1.0). At 0.0 the target is in T-pose. At 1.0 it fully follows source. Intermediate values blend between T-pose and retargeted pose.

## Particle Effects
- When retargeting is active (blend > 0), emit particles from each target joint. Particles are small sprites (0.05 size) colored with a gradient from 0xff6600 to 0xffaa00.
- Particles drift upward (y += random 0.01-0.03 per frame), fade out over 60 frames, max 500 particles alive.
- A 'burst' mode: pressing B triggers a burst of 50 particles from all target joints simultaneously.

## UI Controls (DOM overlay)
- A panel at top-left with:
  - 'Speed' slider (0.0 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) controlling animation speed.
  - 'Blend' slider (0.0 to 1.0, step 0.05, default 1.0) controlling retarget blend factor.
  - 'Play/Pause' button toggling animation playback.
  - 'Reset Pose' button that sets blend to 0 and pauses animation.
  - A label showing current frame count (integer, increments each animation frame when playing).
  - 'Particle Count' label showing current live particle count.

## Keyboard Controls
- Space: toggle play/pause.
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown: increase/decrease speed by 0.1 (clamped 0.0-3.0).
- ArrowLeft/ArrowRight: decrease/increase blend by 0.05 (clamped 0.0-1.0).
- B: trigger particle burst.
- R: reset pose (same as Reset Pose button).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
- isPlaying (boolean)
- speed (number, current speed multiplier)
- blendFactor (number, current retarget blend)
- frameCount (integer, animation frames elapsed while playing)
- particleCount (integer, live particles)
- sourceBoneCount (integer, number of bones in source skeleton)
- targetBoneCount (integer, number of bones in target skeleton)
- sourceHipY (number, y-position of source hip bone)
- targetHipY (number, y-position of target hip bone)
- sourceLeftArmRotZ (number, z-rotation of source left arm in radians)
- targetLeftArmRotZ (number, z-rotation of target left arm in radians)
- retargetingActive (boolean, true if blend > 0 and isPlaying)
- burstTriggered (boolean, set true on burst frame, false otherwise)
- sourceHeight (number, total height of source skeleton)
- targetHeight (number, total height of target skeleton)
- lastBurstParticleCount (number, particles added in last burst, 0 if no burst)

All numerical state values must be free of NaN and Infinity.
physics_constraints: Bone rotations must be bounded within [-PI, PI]. Particle positions must remain within a bounding box of [-5, 0, -5] to [5, 10, 5]. Particle count must never exceed 500. Speed and blend values must stay clamped to their defined ranges. Retargeted rotations must scale proportionally to blend factor (targetRot ≈ sourceRot * blendFactor within 0.01 tolerance when blend < 1.0).
